## feature

## fix

### Post-commit backup cleanup failure destroyed committed outputs

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: permanent data loss. Backup removal ran inside the rollback scope, so
a failed backup `unlink` after a fully successful publication triggered a
full rollback — deleting the committed outputs and then failing to restore
the already-deleted backups.

#### description

```
type: text
```

1. The publish loop is followed by an explicit commit point: every
   requested output is published and complete.
2. Backup removal after that point is post-commit housekeeping: a failed
   `unlink` collects the leftover `.pairloom-bak-*` paths and reports them
   loudly on stderr; the committed outputs stay in place and the run exits
   0.
3. Failures during publication keep the existing backup/restore rollback
   (unchanged, regression-tested in the previous batch).

#### before

```text
second run (cleanup failure on 2nd backup) exit=1
files after: ['d.parquet.pairloom-bak-…', 's.parquet.pairloom-bak-…']
previous a.bam recoverable: False
```

#### after

```text
second run (cleanup failure on 2nd backup) exit=0
files after: ['a.bam', 'd.parquet', 'd.parquet.pairloom-bak-…', 's.parquet']
previous a.bam recoverable: True
pairmerge: warning: could not remove backup file(s); delete them manually: …
```

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Regression: `tests/test_errors.py::TestPublishIntegrity::test_backup_cleanup_failure_preserves_committed_outputs`
(one-shot `os.unlink` failure on the `d.parquet` backup; asserts exit 0,
all outputs present, the exact leftover backup, and the stderr warning).
:::

### Candidate truncation discarded the original BAM placement

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: truncation silently reduced the pair search's achievable overlap,
changing merge outcomes versus BAM-only discovery for reads whose original
placement fell beyond the candidate cap.

#### description

```
type: text
```

When the leftmost cap-kept set does not contain the BAM's own placement,
the last kept slot is reserved for it; the cap is still honored, the
`truncated` flag and conservative MAPQ are untouched, and the leftmost
slot (orphan normalization) never changes.

#### before

```text
default discovery: unmerged pos=436 … insufficient_overlap (overlap 4)
bam-only discovery: merged: 1                                (overlap 12)
```

#### after

```text
default discovery exit=0; merged: 1   (28M at 444, MAPQ 3)
bam-only discovery exit=0; merged: 1  (parity)
```

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Regression: `tests/test_integration.py::TestPairAwareOptimization::test_truncated_candidates_keep_original_placement`
(20-base reads at 444/452 in the tandem repeat; asserts merge at the
original placement with conservative MAPQ and parity with
`--candidate-source bam`).
:::

### Stale MQ tags survived MAPQ-only adjustments

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: contradictory metadata — the reciprocal mate-MAPQ tag kept its
input value while the record's own MAPQ was conservatively adjusted, for
every unchanged repeat-ambiguous placement.

#### description

```
type: text
```

1. `_sync_mate_fields` sets reciprocal `MQ` from the mates' adjusted
   MAPQs after both placements are applied (covers unchanged placements
   and cross-contig pairs).
2. `_adjust_single` removes `MQ` on the mapped record of an orphan (mate
   unmapped or absent), and refreshes it on the unmapped mate from the
   mapped record's adjusted MAPQ.

#### before

```text
pos=400 mapq=3 MQ=60    (both mates)
```

#### after

```text
pos=400 mapq=3 MQ=3     (both mates)
```

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Regressions: `tests/test_candidates_mapq.py::TestMateMapqPolicy::test_mq_refreshed_when_only_mapq_changes`,
`test_mq_follows_movement`;
`tests/test_classify_policy.py::TestRecordPolicy::test_orphan_stale_mq_removed`.
The batch-2 tagged-move test now pins `MQ == 3` (refreshed) instead of
tag absence.
:::

### Duplicate primary read numbers bypassed pairing validation

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: silent record loss — the later duplicate overwrote the earlier in
the processing slot, which was then tagged with a classification it never
contributed to.

#### description

```
type: text
```

`check_pair_flags` now counts read1/read2 slots across the template's
primaries and raises `DataInvariantError` when either exceeds one,
consistent with the existing more-than-two-primaries check.

#### before

```text
adjust exit=0 (pairing invariant violation should fail loudly => 1)
  pos=500 tags=['ZC']      <- never processed, still tagged
  pos=600 tags=['ZC']
```

#### after

```text
adjust exit=1
pairmerge: error: template 'dup' has duplicate primary read1/read2 records
           (read1=2, read2=0); input violates pairing invariants
```

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Regression: `tests/test_classify_policy.py::TestRecordPolicy::test_duplicate_primary_read_numbers_fail_loudly`
(asserts exit 1 and no published output).
:::

## limitation

### Post-commit cleanup failures leave litter

```
level: low
```

#### reason

Low: the chosen trade-off keeps committed outputs at the cost of possible
leftover backup files, which the warning names explicitly.

#### description

```
type: text
```

A backup that cannot be unlinked after the commit point stays on disk
until removed manually; PairLoom reports the exact paths on stderr.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Pinned by `test_backup_cleanup_failure_preserves_committed_outputs`
(leftover list asserted exactly).
:::

## caveat

### Two intentional behavior changes

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: user-visible semantic changes confirmed this session; recorded so
downstream users are not surprised.

#### description

```
type: text
```

1. `MQ` is now refreshed (or removed for unmapped/absent mates) even on
   unchanged placements — a documented exception to the "unchanged records
   keep their input tags" policy.
2. Templates with duplicate primary read1/read2 records now fail loudly
   (exit 1) instead of silently processing one record.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Both pinned by the regressions above; README states both rules (adjusted
records paragraph, record policy bullet).
:::

status: right
